definition: The layer of gases surrounding the Earth. The modern atmosphere is approximately 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, and 1% argon and other gases.
The most abundant gas in the Earth's atmosphere, making up approximately 78%. It is largely unreactive under normal conditions.
The second most abundant gas in the atmosphere, making up approximately 21%. Produced by photosynthesis and used in respiration and combustion.
A greenhouse gas present in the atmosphere in small amounts (about 0.04%). Produced by combustion, respiration, and volcanic activity. Removed by photosynthesis.
The gradual change in the composition of Earth's atmosphere over billions of years — from volcanic gases (mainly CO₂, water vapour, nitrogen) to the oxygen-rich atmosphere we have today.
The process by which plants use light energy, carbon dioxide, and water to produce glucose and oxygen. Responsible for the rise in oxygen levels in the early atmosphere.
A gas that absorbs and re-emits infrared radiation, trapping heat in the atmosphere. Examples include carbon dioxide, methane, and water vapour.
The process by which greenhouse gases in the atmosphere trap heat energy from the Sun, keeping the Earth warm enough to support life.
The increased warming of the Earth caused by rising levels of greenhouse gases due to human activities such as burning fossil fuels and deforestation.
The gradual increase in the average temperature of the Earth's surface, primarily caused by the enhanced greenhouse effect due to increased greenhouse gas emissions.
Long-term changes in global weather patterns caused by global warming. Effects include rising sea levels, more extreme weather events, and changes to ecosystems.
The total amount of greenhouse gases (especially CO₂) released into the atmosphere as a result of the activities of a person, organisation, or product.
A potent greenhouse gas produced by livestock, landfill sites, rice paddies, and natural gas leaks. More effective at trapping heat than CO₂ per molecule.
Non-renewable energy sources (coal, oil, and natural gas) formed from ancient organisms. Burning fossil fuels releases CO₂ and other pollutants into the atmosphere.
Rain that is more acidic than normal due to dissolved sulfur dioxide (SO₂) and nitrogen oxides (NOₓ) produced by burning fossil fuels. Damages buildings, ecosystems, and aquatic life.
A toxic gas produced when fossil fuels containing sulfur are burned. A major cause of acid rain. Reacts with water and oxygen in the atmosphere to form sulfuric acid.
Gases produced when nitrogen and oxygen from the air react together at the high temperatures inside car engines. Contribute to acid rain and smog.
Tiny solid or liquid particles released into the atmosphere by incomplete combustion of fuels. Can cause respiratory problems and contribute to smog.
A toxic gas produced by the incomplete combustion of carbon-containing fuels. Binds to haemoglobin in red blood cells, preventing oxygen transport.
The large-scale removal of forests. Reduces the amount of CO₂ absorbed by photosynthesis and contributes to increased greenhouse gas levels.
